title: Three Persian words that ended a reign | Folio 2 — The Honest Historian #Shorts
description:
Beyhaqi also gives us a glimpse of Muhammad himself, the young man left behind in the fortress. For two or three days, we are told, he was lost in sorrow and would not speak. A few days later, envoys came up to the fortress with a letter from Masud. Muhammad would stay in Kuhtiz, honorably, with his household, but under guard. When he read it, he grew visibly troubled. And one of the envoys, a wise old official, told him to be patient and accept what God had decided. Then he said three short Persian words. Budani bude ast. What was meant to be, has been. It is a gentle sentence. It is also a door closing.
